page.layout: One block of running text in a single column, full width. No marginal notes, no headings, no footnotes. Printed page number and running head at the top of the page.

main_text.p: Quià Mea Parte ftabant, clarè (crë-do) & indubiè Dei Verbum, & Leges Regni, tùm Iuramenta fua porpria omnia à fe conjunctim ftantia habuerunt: his enim omnibus præcipitur juftis meis Imperiis parere ; nemini certe concedi-ditur extra meum Confenfum, nedum contra me, arma fumere.

. Illi ex parte adverfâ, ad nefcio quas confugiunt prætenfas formidines, & diffolutiffima Statut ( ut vocant ) Fun-damentalia, ea fcilicet quæ præfentem Statum Ecclefiæ & Regni evertunt ; quædam porro hic afferunt Sui in defenfionem argumenta futilia & imaginaria, quæ etiamfi vera effent, minime omnium ab illis urgenda, qui cum mei Subditi effent, Me & Leges meas primi impugnabant, turbas illas initio non coercentes, mox etiam confcripto Exercitu; Ejufmodi certe argumentis, cuicunque Factioni licebit (vires modò adfint & fiducia) quæcunque contra Leges exantes & Magiftratus poftulant, ea Gladio demùm expugnare. Nunquam enim tàm commodè erunt res conftitutæ; ut non aliqui faltem offendantur, & quod Ipfis reformandum videbitur ad Rebellionem ufque profequi incitentur, accedentibus præfertim parafitaftris Concionatoribus, quales hi qui Martyres ap-pellare

page.notes: The running head is printed in Greek capitals; I have read it as ΕΙΚΩΝ ΒΑΣΙΛΙΚΗ. The scan is faint at the word ΒΑΣΙΛΙΚΗ, and the Λ and the final Η are the least certain letters. The stray full stop before "Illi" is as printed. The right edge of the scan is cut off and dark, so the line ends there are read from the visible letters. The line-end hyphens ("concedi-", "quæ-", "ef-", "impugna-", "coercen-", "ex-", "Gla-", "Re-", "ac-", "Con-", "ap-") are printed and kept. The final word "pellare" completes the split word "appellare" and is the last printed line of the page.
